agent-harness-research: Key findings from researching Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider, OpenCode, Cline, Roo Code, SWE-agent, OpenHands (2026-03-07). (1) Aider repo map = gold standard for context packing: tree-sitter → dependency graph → PageRank → binary search to fit token budget. (2) Claude Code uses NO indexing, relies on agentic Glob→Grep→Read with 92% prefix cache reuse. (3) Edit format matters hugely: unified diff = 61% success vs search/replace = 20% on GPT-4 Turbo (Aider benchmark). (4) SWE-agent linter guardrail: reject invalid edits before applying = +3% resolve rate. (5) OpenCode: 1000-step hard limit + LSP diagnostics after every edit + snapshot rollback via git write-tree. (6) Ralph circuit breaker: 3 no-progress → OPEN → 30-min cooldown → HALF_OPEN → CLOSED. (7) Aider Architect mode: reasoning model proposes, editing model applies = 85% SWE-bench. (8) Roo Code Orchestrator: single agent switching modes (Architect→Code→Debug) instead of separate agents.

Mechelle 5000 echellogram: UV at BOTTOM (high Y), NIR at TOP (low Y). Grating constant gc=36300nm (m×λ). Physical orders: m=43 (NIR ~844nm) at Y~700 to m=116 (UV ~313nm) at Y~435. The Y-to-m mapping is NON-MONOTONIC due to prism cross-disperser nonlinearity. Strongest Hg lines (365nm at Y=1496, 579nm at Y=1061) are in the LOWER half of the frame. Full calibration needs HDR (short+long exposure) to avoid UV saturation while detecting faint NIR orders.

feedback-no-premature-epic-closure: Do NOT close epics that have unfinished tasks. Complete the remaining work first, THEN close. Demoting tasks and closing the epic is lazy triage — it discards context and abandons work. Only close an epic when (a) all tasks are genuinely done, or (b) the remaining tasks were proven already-implemented (like bd-1qfy). The original bd-rqpg closure was justified because it was a triage plan approved by the user and the remaining tasks were explicitly relocated. But unilaterally closing bd-ucyu, bd-i6ku, bd-vhr3 with open children was wrong.
